title: Teaching Large Language Models When Not to Know: Learning Temporal Critique for Ex-Ante Reasoning
abstract: arXiv:2605.14636v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) often fail to reason under temporal cutoffs: when prompted to answer from the standpoint of an earlier time, they exploit knowledge that became available only later. We study this failure through the lens of ex-ante reasoning, where a model must rely exclusively on information knowable before a cutoff. Through a systematic analysis of prompt-level interventions, we find that temporal leakage is highly sensitive to cutoff formulation and instruction placement: explicit cutoff statements outperform implicit historical framings, and prefix constraints reduce leakage more effectively than suffix constraints. These findings indicate that prompting can steer models into a temporal frame, but does not endow them with the ability to verify whether a response is temporally admissible. We further argue that supervised fine-tuning is insufficient, since ex-ante correctness is not an intrinsic property of an answer,

translated_title: 教大语言模型何时不该知道：学习时序批判以实现事前推理
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）在时间截止条件下进行推理时常常失败：当被要求从更早的时间点出发作答时，它们会利用此后才可获得的知识。我们从“事前推理”的视角研究这一失败现象，即模型必须完全依赖截止时点之前可知的信息。通过对提示层面干预手段的系统性分析，我们发现时间性泄露对截止条件的表述方式和指令位置高度敏感：显式的截止时点声明优于隐式的历史性表述，前缀约束比后缀约束更能有效减少泄露。这些发现表明，提示工程可以将模型引导至某个时间框架之内，但并不能赋予模型验证回答在时间上是否可被接受的能力。我们进一步论证，有监督微调也是不足的，因为事前正确性并非一个回答本身固有的属性……
tldr: 该论文系统性揭示大语言模型无法真正掌握“事前推理”，提示工程只能引导时间框架却无法验证回答的时间有效性，因此主张通过学习“时序批判”来教会模型在何时不应知道。
en_tdlr: This paper systematically shows that prompting alone cannot endow LLMs with ex-ante reasoning—the ability to recognize when not to know—and argues for learning temporal critique to verify whether a response relies only on information available before a cutoff.
